_readme: Frame and install copy for the customer Frame Types screen. Edit name, bestFor, desc, pros, cons, and installNote. placeholder:true shows the placeholder badge (Settings can hide badges). Retrofit and nailing fin / full frame follow the website. Block frame is not described on the site, so that card stays a placeholder. installType must be an id in data/install.json. Choosing this frame on an estimate line sets that install type and its per-window price. diagram is the picture key: zbar, block, or nailfin. Nick's gallery label 'retrofit / jump frame' is the retrofit card; the site's word is retrofit.

types.name: Retrofit
types.bestFor: Sound stucco homes, especially those built after the mid-1980s, when the old frame can stay.
types.desc: The new window sets into the frame that is already in the wall. The old frame stays. No stucco cut. The glass area is a little smaller. Most retrofit installations finish in a day. On the gallery, Nick's photos of this install are labeled retrofit / jump frame.
pros: The old frame stays in the wall
cons: The old frame has to be solid and close to square
types.installNote: The old sash comes out. The new unit sets inside the existing frame. A Z-shaped fin covers the outside joint.

types.name: Block Frame
types.bestFor: An opening that is already clear — the old frame is gone, or the pocket was built for a plain box frame. The website does not describe this frame, so this card is still a placeholder.
types.desc: A simple box with no fin. It slides into the rough opening and is screwed through the frame into the wall.
pros: No fin to hide or trim around
Easy to shim until it is square
A clean look in a prepared opening
cons: The opening has to be ready — the frame will not cover a missing wall
Outside trim or stucco is a separate step
types.installNote: Set the box in the opening, shim it square, and screw through the jamb. Close the outside edge with trim or a stucco return.

types.name: Full frame / nailing fin
types.bestFor: A full-frame replacement, or new construction before stucco or siding goes on.
types.desc: Full frame takes everything out back to the rough opening, flashing included. It is for a rotted, rusted, or out-of-square frame, a flashing repair, or a change in opening size. Stucco is cut and patched, and that work is part of the quote. Glass area is kept. It takes longer than a retrofit. New construction sets the unit into the framed opening before the outside skin, and the fin is sealed into the weather barrier. If stucco is coming off an elevation anyway, that elevation should get nail-fin units, flashed, before the new lath goes on.
pros: Glass area is kept on a full-frame replacement
The fin gives flashing a place to tie in
The right frame when the wall face is open
cons: Stucco is cut and patched on a replacement
Does not mount over a frame you are keeping
types.installNote: The old frame comes out first on a replacement. Nail the fin to the sheathing, flash it, then let stucco or siding cover the fin.
